content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Name a book, pen, desk, chair, board, and bag with a or an. Model: “There is a blue book on Mai's desk.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use things in the classroom clearly and politely. One useful response is: “There is a blue book on Mai's desk.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where things in the classroom is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?
content_sections.title: Use it

exercises.prompt: Complete the natural sentence about things in the classroom: There is _____ on Mai's desk.
Put these two parts in a natural order to make a message about things in the classroom.
Make a short, personal response about things in the classroom. Use the lesson language and add one detail that is yours.

criteria: The response communicates a clear meaning about things in the classroom.
The response uses the allocated language in an understandable form.
The response adds an appropriate personal or invented detail.

language_focus: Name a book, pen, desk, chair, board, and bag with a or an.
objectives: Name a book, pen, desk, chair, board, and bag with a or an.
Use classroom objects in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about things in the classroom.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about things in the classroom. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: Which item uses an?
listening.transcript: Please put an eraser and a pen on the desk.

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Link an eraser and keep the /n/ sound at the start of an. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Link an eraser and keep the /n/ sound at the start of an.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about things in the classroom.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using things in the classroom; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise things in the classroom?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: There is a blue book on Mai's desk.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about things in the classroom with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about things in the classroom. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: There is a blue book on Mai's desk. Submit your draft first.

title: Things in the classroom
